name: e2e-unreachable
description: Profile for the leg that proves a target which never answers is reported as CONNECTIVITY, not as capacity. Uses an example domain — and resolves it, via bypass, to a loopback port where nothing listens.
_why_bypass_comment: www.example.test cannot resolve (RFC 6761 reserves .test and guarantees it is not in the global DNS), but a resolver that hijacks NXDOMAIN would hand us somebody else's address — and then this test would generate load against a stranger. The bypass removes DNS from the question entirely: the host stays www.example.test for SNI, Host and the allowlist, while the connection goes to 127.0.0.1:9, where nothing listens. Refused instantly, every time, on infrastructure that is ours.
_slo_comment: The brake DOES fire here, and that is the point. A failed rate of exactly 1.0 is not < 1.0, so the threshold crosses — and the report must still say TARGET NEVER ANSWERED rather than presenting the abort as a knee. That precedence is what this leg proves end to end: two flags set, one honest conclusion.
